title: Q289: muscle fibre direction and documented intramuscular septa / aponeuroses for the simulated ultrasound (private clinical add-on)
generated_by: hand-curated (septa, parts, references); the per-muscle pennation table is merged in by scripts/clinical/q289_architecture.py from data/muscles/*/*.json
honesty: Fibre DIRECTION is built from this page's own geometry: the muscle mesh's own principal axes (PCA of its vertices) give the line of action (long axis), the width and the thickness directions. The pennation ANGLE comes from published architecture data (the per-muscle source line, e.g. Ward 2009 lower limb, Holzbaur 2005 upper limb, van Eijden 1997 masseter). How the fibres are laid out inside the mesh (which side, which way they converge) is a RULE, badged as rule-based -- it is not a measured fibre field of this body.

Septa / aponeuroses are drawn ONLY for the muscles listed under 'muscles' below, each with its citation. Their presence is documented; their position, orientation and extent inside this body's mesh are rule-based (stated per entry). Counts are drawn only where a source gives one.

A muscle without an entry in the pennation table shows only the generic line of action (the mesh's own long axis, the Q228 perimysium texture), labelled 'generic line of action, no architecture data'.

rules.frame: a = the mesh's first principal axis oriented proximal -> distal (the end nearer the trunk is proximal), w = second (width), t = third (thickness); c = vertex centroid; extents = vertex projections
rules.unipennate: fibres at the pennation angle in the a-t plane: f = cos(p) a + sin(p) t
rules.bipennate: fibres at +/- the pennation angle in the a-w plane, converging distally on the central sheet: f = cos(p) a - sin(p) sign(d) w, d = signed distance to the sheet
rules.multipennate: between neighbouring sheets the sign of the w component alternates
rules.layered: a sheet across the thickness; fibres at the pennation angle in the a-t plane with opposite signs on the two sides
rules.septum: a hyperechoic sheet 1 mm thick (Gaussian half-width 0.6 mm), only inside the muscle class, only within its span along a

render.note: a septum multiplies the muscle's backscatter by 1 + gain * exp(-(d / half)^2) (d = distance to the sheet): +8.5 dB at its centre, i.e. a hyperechoic line like a tendon; synthetic display constant, not a measured reflectivity

septa.name: central aponeurosis (internal tendon)
septa.rule: drawn as the sheet that splits the muscle across its width, over its whole length; the sources document a central aponeurosis with fascicles on both sides, not its exact position in this body

septa.name: deep intramuscular tendon of the indirect head (central aponeurosis)
septa.rule: drawn mid-width from 5 % to 75 % of the muscle length; the source documents a deep intramuscular tendon making the bipennate portion, not its extent in this body

septa.name: central tendon (intramuscular)
septa.rule: drawn mid-width over the distal 65 %; the anterior / posterior / medial / lateral aponeuroses lie on the muscle's own surfaces, which the simulation already images as interfaces

parts.rule: the medial and lateral heads as the two halves of the mesh across its width (the head on the body-midline side is medial); each half gets its own head's pennation

aponeuroses_note.text: superficial and deep aponeuroses (fascicles between them, unipennate) lie on the mesh's own surfaces and are imaged as interfaces; not drawn again inside

parts.rule: the three parts as thirds of the mesh's width, anterior = the third on the body's anterior side; each third gets its own compartments' pennation

septa.name: intramuscular tendons (seven segments)
septa.rule: seven segments (Sakoma 2011) = six internal sheets, evenly across the width, alternately reaching from the origin side and from the humeral side; positions and spans are rule-based

septa.name: aponeurotic boundary between superficial and deep heads
septa.rule: one sheet at mid-thickness for the superficial / deep head division; the multiple laminae within each head are documented but their number is not given in the source's abstract, so they are NOT drawn

septa.name: intramuscular tendinous portion (anterior half)
septa.rule: drawn at three quarters of the width toward the anterior side, over the lateral (distal) 60 %; the source places it in the anterior half, the exact position is rule-based

septa.name: intramuscular tendinous portion (superior half)
septa.rule: drawn at three quarters of the width toward the superior side, over the lateral (distal) 60 %; the source places it in the superior half, the exact position is rule-based
